title: The Sizes of All the Groups

concept.title: The size of a component is the number of nodes the search reaches from its first node
body: In the component search, the queue of a search holds **exactly the nodes of one component** when it ends. So the size of the component is simply the **length of the queue** at the end of the search. Collect the sizes of all the components in a list, then sort it.

The sizes always add up to `n` (every node is in exactly one component), which is a quick check. The largest component is called the *giant component* in networks, and the number of components of each size is a useful way to describe a network.

statement: An undirected graph has `n` nodes and `m` edges. Print the sizes of all its connected components in non-increasing order (a node without edges is a component of size 1).
inputFormat: The first line has `n` and `m`: the number of nodes (numbered 1 to n) and the number of edges.
Each of the next `m` lines has two numbers `u` and `v`: an edge between the nodes `u` and `v`.
outputFormat: The sizes on one line, from the largest to the smallest.
constraints: There are no self-loops and no repeated edges.
hints: After a search from a new node, the queue contains exactly its component.
Remember the length of the queue as the size of the component.
Sort all the sizes from the largest to the smallest.

input = sys.stdin.readline

n, m = map(int, input().split())
edges = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(m)]

explanation: After a search from each new node the queue is exactly one component, so its length is the size; the sizes are sorted from the largest to the smallest.
solution.complexity: Time O(n + m + c log c) for c components, space O(n + m).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, m = map(int, input().split())
edges = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(m)]

adj = [[] for _ in range(n + 1)]
for u, v in edges:
    adj[u].append(v)
    adj[v].append(u)
sizes = []
seen = [False] * (n + 1)
for start in range(1, n + 1):
    if seen[start]:
        continue
    seen[start] = True
    queue = [start]
    for v in queue:
        for w in adj[v]:
            if not seen[w]:
                seen[w] = True
                queue.append(w)
    sizes.append(len(queue))
sizes.sort(reverse=True)
print(*sizes)
